instruction: Create a one-slide PPT based on the image. Every element must be editable, the size must match the image, and the circled parts must be changed to straight lines.

dim1: The deliverable is in .ppt or .pptx format and can be opened normally.
The delivered PPT contains 1 slide featuring the chemical reaction scheme, and the slide can be opened normally in edit mode.

On the slide featuring the reaction scheme, all molecular structures, atomic symbols, chemical formulas, plus signs, reaction arrows, and connecting lines are individually selectable and editable PowerPoint objects; a full-slide screenshot, a single whole image, or a non-editable bitmap must not be used as a substitute.

On the slide featuring the reaction scheme, the background is pure white or nearly white. The entire chemical reaction diagram fills the slide without changing its aspect ratio, with minimal blank space on the left, right, top, and bottom, and is centered on the slide overall.

On the slide featuring the reaction scheme, both the top group and the bottom group of reaction schemes are shown in full, and both positions marked with red circles have been changed to straight-line connections, with no parallel double lines, triple lines, wavy lines, or bent lines.

On the slide featuring the reaction scheme, all text and line segments are clearly visible, with no obvious overlap, cropping, objects extending beyond the slide boundaries, missing structures, or blank space exceeding 40% of the area.

Apart from the slide featuring the reaction scheme, all other slides can be opened normally, with no completely blank slides, slides containing only the background, or large areas where objects have disappeared.
dim2: +5: Overall composition of the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Two complete groups of chemical reaction schemes appear on the slide, with the first-step reaction at the top and the second-step reaction at the bottom. The overall composition matches the reference image and extends horizontally, occupying 85%—96% of the usable slide width and 70%—88% of the usable slide height. The entire chemical reaction diagram is enlarged proportionally without changing its aspect ratio. The left edge of the chemical formula is approximately 0-0.3 cm from the left edge of the slide, the right edge of the chemical formula is approximately 0.2-0.6 cm from the right edge of the slide, the top edge of the chemical formula is approximately 0.4-1 cm from the top edge of the slide, and the bottom edge of the chemical formula is approximately 3-4 cm from the bottom edge of the slide. The slide background is white, with no gradient, texture, background image, watermark, or annotation marks.

+3: Upper-left reactant structure on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the upper-left area of the slide, approximately 10-11 cm wide and 5-5.5 cm high; includes a six-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle with vertically opposing nitrogen atoms, “Cl” at the lower left, a side chain at the upper right, and terminal “Cl”. The structural lines form a vertically oriented equilateral hexagon, with two “N” labels at the top and bottom vertices of the hexagon. Inside the hexagon are two diagonal lines at the upper right between points 1 and 2 and at the lower right between points 3 and 4, and one vertical line on the left between points 5 and 6. A downward-opening bent line at point 2 and a straight line at point 5 each connect to a “Cl”.

+1: Text in the upper-left reactant on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Letters such as “N” and “Cl” in the structure are all editable text, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 30-32 pt, and black.

+1: Bond lines in the upper-left reactant on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: The six-membered ring edges, side-chain lines, and terminal connecting lines are all solid black lines, approximately 0.75—1.25 pt wide, and are all editable straight-line objects.

+1: 1st plus sign at the top of the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the middle to the right of the upper-left reactant. The text is “+”, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 32-34 pt, and black.

+1: Chemical formula of the upper-middle reactant on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located to the right of the 1st plus sign. The text is “(CH₃)₂NH” or an equivalent subscript format, approximately 5.3-5.5 cm wide and 1.2-1.4 cm high, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 32-34 pt, and black.

+1: Upper reaction arrow on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located to the right of the upper-middle reactant, approximately 4.7-5 cm long, pointing from left to right, with a line width of approximately 0.75—1.25 pt and a clearly visible arrowhead; it is an editable straight arrow overall.

+3: Upper-right product structure on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the upper-right area of the slide, approximately 11.5-12 cm wide and 6.0-6.5 cm high; includes a six-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle on the left, “Cl” at the lower left, a middle side chain, and a dimethylamino structure at the right end.

+1: Line modification requirement for the upper-right product on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: A single solid black line appears between the right-side chain of the heterocycle and the nitrogen-containing substituent at the right end; there are no two parallel lines and no triple-bond style.

+1: Text in the upper-right product on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Letters such as “N” and “Cl” in the structure are all editable text, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 30-32 pt, and black.

+3: Lower-left reactant structure on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the lower-left area of the slide, approximately 11.4-12 cm wide and 5.8-6.3 cm high; overall similar to the upper-right product structure, including a six-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle on the left, “Cl” at the lower left, a middle side chain, and a dimethylamino structure at the right end.

+1: Line modification requirement for the lower-left reactant on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: A single solid black line appears between the right-side chain of the heterocycle and the nitrogen-containing substituent at the right end; there are no two parallel lines and no triple-bond style.

+1: Text in the lower-left reactant on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Letters such as “N” and “Cl” in the structure are all editable text, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 32-34 pt, and black.

+1: 2nd plus sign at the bottom of the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the middle to the right of the lower-left reactant. The text is “+”, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 32-34 pt, and black.

+5: Lower-middle reagent structure on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the lower-middle area of the slide, approximately 8.2-8.7 cm wide and 8.5-9.2 cm high; includes a five-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle at the top, a central carbonyl “O”, “H₃C” at the bottom, and an “O—CH₃” structure at the lower right. For the positions of the lines and letters, there is one “N” at each of top point 1, lower-right point 3, and upper-left point 5 of the five-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle. There is one short line between points 2 and 3 and another between points 5 and 1. A short line extends diagonally downward from point 4 and connects to an “O”. Below the “O” are two parallel short lines whose other ends extend respectively to “H₃C” at the lower left and “O—CH₃” at the lower right.

+1: Text in the lower-middle reagent on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: “N”, “O”, “H₃C”, “O—CH₃”, and similar labels are all editable text, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 26-28 pt, and black.

+1: Lower reaction arrow on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located to the right of the lower-middle reagent, approximately 4.7-5 cm long, pointing from left to right, with a line width of approximately 0.75—1.25 pt and a clearly visible arrowhead.

+5: Lower-right product structure on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Located in the lower-right area of the slide, approximately 14.3-14.6 cm wide and 10-10.5 cm high; includes a six-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle on the left, “Cl” at the lower left, a middle chain connection, a central nitrogen-containing linking group, a nitrogen-containing five-membered ring on the right, and a carbonyl “O”.

+1: Text in the lower-right product on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: Letters such as “N”, “Cl”, and “O” in the structure are all editable text, in Times New Roman or Cambria Math, approximately 30-32 pt, and black.

+1: Bond lines in the lower-right product on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: The molecular skeleton, heterocycle edges, carbonyl double lines, and connecting lines are all solid black lines, approximately 0.75—1.25 pt wide, and are all editable straight-line objects.

+3: Text consistency of the chemical structures on the slide featuring the reaction scheme: All atomic symbols, chemical formulas, plus signs, and any subscripts throughout the slide use a consistent font system, with font-size differences not exceeding 4 pt, and are all black. All chemical bond lines, reaction arrows, and structural outlines throughout the slide use a consistent black color, with line widths consistently between 0.75—1.25 pt.

+5: Editability of the slide featuring the reaction scheme: The user can separately select the upper-left reactant structure line segments, upper-middle chemical formula, upper arrow, upper-right product structure, lower-left reactant structure, lower-middle reagent structure, lower arrow, and lower-right product structure, and modify or delete each independently.
